title: Understanding Anxiety Basics
summary: This quiz covers common types, symptoms, causes, and risk factors for anxiety disorders. It also reviews diagnosis, treatment options, coping skills, and support for daily life.

questions.q: Which of these is a commonly recommended first way to calm anxiety in the moment?
o: Drink several cups of strong coffee to stay alert
Take fast, shallow chest breaths to get more air
Do slow, deep belly breathing for a few minutes
Stay in bed alone all day to avoid all stress
questions.tip: Slow, controlled breathing helps activate the body's calming response and is widely recommended for coping with anxiety in the moment.
questions.eli5: Think of it like letting air out of a balloon slowly instead of popping it. Steady breaths tell your body the alarm can turn down.

questions.q: What is the key feature that turns normal worry into an anxiety disorder?
o: Brief nervousness before a big test that goes away afterward
Persistent, excessive fear or worry that interferes with daily life
Feeling calm and focused during stressful times
A short burst of excitement before a fun event
questions.tip: Anxiety disorders involve persistent excessive fear or worry that interferes with daily life.
questions.eli5: Like a school fire alarm that keeps ringing all day even with no fire, it makes it hard to do normal classwork.

questions.q: Which pattern best describes generalized anxiety disorder, meaning constant worry about many everyday topics?
o: Excessive worry about many everyday events, more days than not for at least six months, that is hard to control
Sudden episodes of intense fear that peak within minutes for no clear reason
Extreme fear only of social situations like meeting new people
A specific unrealistic fear of one object, such as spiders
questions.tip: Generalized anxiety disorder involves excessive worry about everyday events occurring more days than not for at least six months and feeling hard to control.
questions.eli5: Like worrying about homework, chores, and shopping every single day for months, like carrying too many heavy grocery bags at once.

questions.q: Which experience best fits panic disorder, which involves sudden attacks of intense fear?
o: Slowly building worry about bills and work over many months
Shyness that fades after getting to know classmates
A realistic fear during a truly dangerous emergency
A sudden episode of intense fear with sweating, chest pain, and a pounding heartbeat, even with no clear danger
questions.tip: Panic disorder involves sudden episodes of intense fear that can occur without an apparent reason, often with sweating, chest pain, and a pounding heartbeat.
questions.eli5: Like a cooking timer blasting suddenly when nothing is in the oven, your body acts alarmed for no clear reason.

questions.q: Which example best shows social anxiety disorder, which is strong fear of social situations?
o: Preferring to stay home sometimes but still enjoying parties and meetings
Feeling a little nervous before a speech but then speaking anyway
Extreme fear of being judged in social situations, leading to avoiding parties, speaking up, or eating in front of others
Disliking one food but being comfortable around other people
questions.tip: Social anxiety disorder involves extreme fear and avoidance of social situations.
questions.eli5: Like being so afraid of spilling food at a family dinner that you skip dinner altogether to avoid being watched.

questions.q: What is the difference between a specific phobia and agoraphobia?

A specific phobia is fear of open places, while agoraphobia is fear of one animal
A specific phobia lasts only seconds, while agoraphobia never involves fear
A specific phobia is normal caution, while agoraphobia is enjoyment of crowds
questions.tip: Specific phobia is a specific unrealistic fear of an object or situation, while agoraphobia is intense fear and avoidance of situations where escape might be difficult.
questions.eli5: Like being scared of one spider in the kitchen versus being scared to go shopping at all in case you cannot leave the store quickly.

questions.q: Which set of signs is most typical of an anxiety disorder?
o: Occasional happiness and deep relaxation with no tension
Forgetting a name once and then remembering it later
Brief excitement before a fun game that quickly passes
Persistent worrying, restlessness, and physical signs such as a faster heartbeat
questions.tip: Symptoms of anxiety disorders can include persistent worrying, restlessness, and physical signs such as increased heart rate.
questions.eli5: Like a school backpack that stays heavy all day with worry, fidgeting, and a racing heart, not just heavy for one minute.

questions.q: Which pattern best describes generalized anxiety disorder (ongoing excessive worry)?

Ongoing hard-to-control worry about many everyday topics like work, health, and money
Extreme fear and avoidance of social situations like parties
Intense fear of one specific object or situation like spiders
questions.tip: Generalized anxiety disorder involves chronic excessive worry about many everyday issues without a single specific trigger.
questions.eli5: It is like carrying a heavy backpack of worries about school, family, and chores all at once, not just one thing.

questions.q: For how long must hard-to-control worry occur on most days to fit generalized anxiety disorder?
o: For at least two weeks
For at least one month
For at least three months
On more days than not for at least six months
questions.tip: Generalized anxiety disorder involves excessive worry occurring more days than not for at least six months.
questions.eli5: Think of it like a long rainy season that lasts half a year, not just a few rainy days.

questions.q: How is generalized anxiety disorder different from a specific phobia?
o: GAD is worry about many everyday issues, while a phobia is an unrealistic fear of one specific object or situation
GAD only happens in brief panic attacks, while a phobia lasts for months without stopping
GAD is fear of social situations, while a phobia is fear of open spaces where escape is hard
GAD has no emotional symptoms, while a phobia causes only physical symptoms
questions.tip: Generalized anxiety disorder involves broad worry about many topics, while specific phobia involves fear tied to one specific object or situation.
questions.eli5: GAD is like worrying about the whole shopping list, while a phobia is like being scared of just the freezer aisle.

questions.q: Which set of symptoms is most typical of generalized anxiety disorder?

Ongoing worrying, restlessness, and physical signs like a faster heart rate

questions.eli5: It is like trying to do homework while a loud TV keeps playing — you cannot turn it off and schoolwork gets harder.

Taking daily antibiotics to cure worry
Avoiding all people and responsibilities permanently
Drinking more caffeine and energy drinks to stay alert

questions.eli5: It is like learning a new cooking recipe for your thoughts — you practice calmer steps with a coach until they feel normal.

A low mood and loss of interest that lasts for weeks
A sudden episode of intense fear that peaks quickly and can happen without a clear reason
A fear that only happens when facing a specific animal like a spider

Feeling calm and keeping the same daily routine with no changes
Ongoing worry about having another attack and avoiding places where leaving or getting help might be hard
questions.tip: People with panic disorder often fear future attacks and avoid situations where escape might be difficult.

questions.q: Which statement best separates panic disorder from a specific phobia?
o: Both conditions are triggered by exactly the same specific object every time

A specific phobia causes unexpected attacks and panic disorder never involves sudden fear

questions.eli5: Like a phone ringing loudly out of nowhere compared to a phone that only rings when grandma calls.

questions.q: Which treatment approach follows mainstream guidance for panic disorder?
o: Cognitive behavioral therapy to change unhelpful thought patterns, sometimes combined with medicines, plus better sleep, stress management, and limiting caffeine
Taking antibiotics alone for a few days to cure panic attacks
Staying alone in bed for months with no activity and no professional help
Drinking more coffee and energy drinks and getting less sleep to push through stress
questions.tip: Cognitive behavioral therapy that addresses negative thought patterns is first-line for anxiety, sometimes with medicines, plus sleep, stress management, and limiting caffeine.
questions.eli5: Like learning a new cooking recipe step by step with a teacher, plus getting good rest instead of too much coffee.

o: Fear of sudden intense panic that comes without any clear reason
Fear of being judged, embarrassed, or rejected when watched by others
Fear of one specific object, such as dogs or spiders
Worry about many everyday topics like money, health, and work

o: Everyone will think I sound stupid and laugh at me if I speak up
I worry about many different everyday problems and cannot control it

o: Sudden sweating, chest pain, and pounding heart at home with no clear trigger
Excessive hard-to-control worry about many everyday events for months
Intense fear of a specific animal that is avoided whenever possible

questions.tip: In social anxiety, feared social scrutiny triggers physical signs like blushing, trembling, sweating, and fast heartbeat.

questions.q: How is social anxiety disorder different from ordinary shyness?
o: It is mild nervousness that goes away quickly after saying hello

A specific phobia involves worry about many everyday topics, while social anxiety involves only spiders.

There is no difference; both mean the same fear of heights.
questions.tip: Specific phobia centers on a particular object or situation, while social anxiety centers on scrutiny and embarrassment in social situations.

questions.q: Which example best shows agoraphobia, meaning intense fear and avoidance of places where escape might be difficult?
o: A person who washes hands many times a day for fear of germs
A person who avoids basements because of a strong fear of spiders
A person who avoids crowded buses, malls, and open squares and stays home unless someone goes along
A person who worries all day about bills, health, and work without one clear trigger
questions.tip: Agoraphobia involves intense fear and avoidance of situations where escape might be difficult or help might be unavailable.

questions.q: What is the central fear in agoraphobia?

Being judged, embarrassed, or rejected by other people in social situations
Being harmed by a specific animal or object, such as dogs or blood
Worrying too much about many everyday problems for months at a time

Staying home and avoiding all feared places until the fear disappears on its own
Increasing caffeine and using willpower alone to push through panic

questions.eli5: Like learning to swim by starting in the shallow end with a coach, not by never going near water.

Women are more likely than men
